item.title: Pune GM Round Robin 2026 begins tomorrow at The Fern Habitat
item.description: The Title norm hunt has long been the most expensive hurdle for aspiring Indian Grandmasters- but Pune is about to rewrite that script after Tamil Nadu. From June 30th to July 8th, 2026, the inaugural Pune International Grandmaster Round Robin Tournament is bringing the titleholders from globe right to Maharashtra's doorstep. This historic event merges the decades-long grassroots dedication of the Kunte family’s Buddhibal Kreeda Trust with the modern, inclusive hospitality of Balraj Singh Ghai’sThe Fern Habitat. This powerhouse collaboration is cutting down travel costs by 80% and proving that Indian chess is ready to claim its home-court advantage.

item.title: The Big Chess Inter-School Tournament returns to Mumbai on 4th & 5th July 2026
item.description: The Big Chess Inter-School Tournament returns for its third edition on 4th and 5th July 2026 at Dublin Square, Phoenix Marketcity Mall, Mumbai. Open to school-going children up to 10th standard, the tournament promises exciting competition, attractive prizes, scholarships, and a chance to play a simul against a GM/IM. Registrations are now open, with limited spots available in each category. Read the full article to know all the details and register before entries close.

item.title: Zero Fees, Zero Prizes: The Movement Changing Kerala Chess
item.description: Great movements often begin with a simple question: What if every aspiring player, irrespective of financial background, had an opportunity to experience serious classical chess? That was the question that gave 1st Chess For Everyone by Premier Chess Academy. When the inaugural edition took place in Thiruvananthapuram back in March 2026, it felt like a bold experiment. A FIDE-rated classical tournament with exactly ₹0 entry fee and ₹0 cash prize. Premier Chess Academy is coming up with its 2nd Chess for Everyone tournament from 20th to 23rd August. Read more about this initiative.

item.title: Arkady Dvorkovich to seek third term as FIDE President
item.description: With two people already having announced their willingness to run for the post of FIDE President -Wadim RosensteinandJan Buettner, it was now time for the incumbent FIDE President Arkady Dvorkovich to announce his willingness to seek the post of FIDE President for the third term. Viswanathan Anand will no longer be the one who become the Deputy President if Dvorkovich wins. It would be Timur Turlov.

item.title: Magnus Carlsen will come to India for the Global Chess League Season 4
item.description: The Global Chess League is one of the best team tournaments in the world of chess. Some of the best players in the world play in the event. This year the 4th edition will take place in Bangalore, India from the 3rd to 13th of September 2026. Magnus Carlsen will make a return to the competition after not playing in the 2025 edition. 29th of June 2026 is when the players will be drafted in the respective teams. We tell you who are the players in the draft.

item.title: Harshavardhan G.B. Becomes India’s 97th Grandmaster
item.description: Harshavardhan G.B. is India's 97th Grandmaster. He has scored his final Grandmaster norm at the 2nd Chola Chess GM Norm Round Robin Tournament, officially securing his GM title. He remained completely unbeaten throughout the tournament, scoring the required 6.5/9 points, and crossing 2500 rating too!! His path to the final norm was an absolute masterclass in clutch performance. After sitting on 3 points from the first 5 rounds, he needed an intense 3.5 points from his final 4 games to cross the finish line. Check out what happened next. Photos: Devansh Singh

item.title: Final Round Showdown: High-Stakes Battle for GM and IM Norms in Chennai
item.description: IM Harshavardhan G B is just half a point away from becoming the 97th Grandmaster of India. Harshavardhan already has 2 GM Norms, and in this Chola Chess GM Norm Round Robin Tournament, his live rating went above 2500. A draw is enough for him to secure his final GM Norm. In the penultimate round, he defeated GM Alexei Fedorov with black pieces, and in the final round, he is facing GM Mihail Nikitenko with white pieces. Photos: Devansh Singh

item.title: HelpChess Foundation raises Rs. 80 Lakh in 2025–26 to support chess players
item.description: The HelpChess Foundation has raised Rs. 80,83,155 in the year 2025-26 through 936 contributions received from the chess community. These funds were directed towards supporting talented chess players across India. This article provides a detailed account of the beneficiaries, their achievements, and how the funds were utilized. Read the full report to understand how every contribution helped strengthen and grow the chess ecosystem.

item.title: Ashutosh Banerjee Wins 4th Gujarat GM Below 2000 Rating 2026
item.description: Ashutosh Banerjee scored 8.5/10 points to win the 4th Gujarat International Open Grandmasters Chess Tournament-2026 (Category B - Below 2000). Vivek Sharma and Shreyas Ghadi also scored 8.5/10 points to secure 2nd and 3rd place according to tiebreak scores. The tournament was held at Veer Savarkar Sports Complex, Ahmedabad, from 1st to 4th June 2026. The total prize fund was ₹15,00,000 with the top 3 prizes of ₹1,25,000, ₹1,00,000, and ₹80,000. Photos: Mr. Bhavesh Patel

item.title: Felix Blohberger Wins Friendly Match Against David Navara in Vienna
item.description: From June 8 to 13, a fascinating friendly match took place in Vienna, Austria, between 23-year-old Austrian Grandmaster Felix Blohberger and renowned Czech Grandmaster David Navara, a former 2750+ player and for many years the leading player of the Czech Republic. The match ended with a 3.5-2.5 victory for Blohberger and marks an important milestone in the Austrian grandmaster’s journey toward the 2600 mark, a goal he has set for himself. Photos:Emilia loren

item.title: World Youth Chess Championship Concludes in Grand Style Six New Champions Crowned
item.description: The FIDE World Youth Chess Championships 2026 concluded with six new World Champions emerging across the age categories. IM Anthony Atanasov of Canada (Open Under-18), WFM Valeria Kleymenova of FIDE (Girls Under-18), IM Khagan Ahmad of Azerbaijan (Open Under-16), WFM Veranika Abramkina of FIDE (Girls Under-16), FM Antoni Radzimski of Poland (Open Under-14), and Zahra Allahverdi of Azerbaijan (Girls Under-14) captured the coveted world titles.

item.title: Harshavardhan G B, Aarit Kapil and Daakshin Arun in Race to Score Norms
item.description: 7 rounds are completed at the Chola Chess IM and GM Norm Round Robin Tournament, and after 7 days of intense games and decisive results, only 3 players are left in the race to score IM and GM norms. In the GM Group, Harshavardhan G B scored a big win over tournament leader Michal Krasenkow, and now he has to score 1.5/2 to score his GM norm. In IM Group, Aarit Kapil needs 1 point in the last 2 games while Daakshin Arun needs 1.5. The next 2 days will be packed with action at Chola Chess, Chennai. Photos: Devansh Singh

item.title: Wadim Rosenstein to run for the post of FIDE President
item.description: Wadim Rosenstein has announced his candidacy for Presidency of FIDE through a post on X. 26th June 2026 is the day when people can annoucne their Candidacy and Wadim has made his announcement. Another person who has also joined the presidency race isJan Henric Buettner. Read more about Wadim's plans related to FIDE Presidency.

item.title: Jan Henric Buettner Announces Candidacy for the Presidency of FIDE
item.description: The race for the FIDE Presidentship is getting very exciting. Two people have already announced that they will be running for the top spot of chess governance -Wadim Rosensteinand Jan Buettner. In this article we present to you the press release shared by Jan Henric Buettner and his team.

item.title: Jagreet Misra Prevails at 2nd Bina Refinery's Project Lakshya Rapid Rating 2026
item.description: Candidate Master Jagreet Misra scored an unbeaten 8.5/9 points to win the 2nd BPCL Bina Refinery's Project Lakshya Rapid Rating Chess Tournament 2026. Vedant Bharadwaj of Madhya Pradesh scored 8/9 points to secure 2nd place. 4 players scored 7.5/9 to finish in 3rd to 6th place. The tournament was organised at Punjabi Bhavan, Bina, Madhya Pradesh, on 6th and 7th June. The total prize fund was ₹1,50,000, with the top 3 prizes of ₹15,000, ₹11,000, and ₹8,000 respectively. Photos: IA Yashpal Arora
